cards.name: Note
cards.text: The 3-4 words that define this game and every decision gets checked against them (e.g. "tense, tactical, readable at a glance"). Written FIRST, before any art — a pillar you can't point to when reviewing an asset isn't actually guiding anything.

cards.name: Note
cards.text: Early exploration sketches and mood pieces for characters, environments, and key props. Mark clearly which concepts are approved vs. still exploratory — an unmarked "maybe" concept has a way of quietly becoming the final direction by accident.

cards.name: Note
cards.text: Visual pillars: color palette, silhouette language, stylization level vs. realism, and 2-3 reference games/films that define the target look — specific enough that a new artist joining mid-project can match it without guessing.

cards.name: Note
cards.text: Blockout the level in basic shapes BEFORE any final art — verify scale, sightlines, and pacing with a real playtest first. Real-world locations, other games' layouts, and pacing references (where players rest vs. where the action ramps up) belong here.

cards.name: Note
cards.text: Silhouettes first (a character should read from a pure black shape alone), then turnarounds, expression sheets, and outfit/variant references. Mark which characters are player-facing hero assets vs. background NPCs — the budget for each is completely different.

cards.name: Note
cards.text: Master list of required assets (props, characters, environment kits) ordered by what BLOCKS other work vs. what can be polished last. A missing placeholder asset stalls a whole level; a rough-but-present hero character doesn't.

cards.name: Note
cards.text: Target platform(s), poly budget per asset type, texture resolution/atlas rules, draw-call budget, and engine-specific limits (Unity/Unreal shader constraints, mobile GPU limits). Set this BEFORE production art starts — redoing 200 assets to hit a budget found late is the most expensive mistake in game art.

cards.name: Note
cards.text: HUD layout references, menu flow diagrams, and accessibility notes (colorblind modes, text scaling, control remapping) — UI is a first-class production discipline here, not an afterthought bolted on at the end.

cards.name: Note
cards.text: Drop concept art (image cards) and the actual greybox/blockout (a .glb/.fbx/.obj 3D model card) here as they land — this column is what "greybox before final art" from the sections on the left is actually tracking against.
